VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_opf.add_base_control_effort(prob: PulpLpModel | OrToolsLpModel, t_idx: int, branch_data_t: PassiveBranchData, active_branch_data_t: ActiveBranchData, branch_vars: BranchVariables, vsc_vars: ConverterVariables, hvdc_vars: ConverterVariables, effort: List[LpAffineExpression | LinearExpr]) → None[source]

Append the N-state control effort terms in p.u. of power.

Phase shifter angles and free converter powers carry no cost in the transfer objective, so many operating points reach the same TTC. Their effort is the flow shifted by the angle change (|Δτ| / X) and the converter power |P|. Each term is weighted 1 + 1e-3 x device index, so equal effort alternatives (e.g. two identical corridors) resolve to the same device in every run.

Parameters:

  • prob – linear problem the effort variables are added to

  • t_idx – time index being formulated

  • branch_data_t – passive branch data, for the phase shifter reactance

  • active_branch_data_t – active branch data, for the scheduled tap angles

  • branch_vars – branch LP variable container

  • vsc_vars – VSC LP variable container

  • hvdc_vars – HVDC LP variable container

  • effort – output list the weighted absolute-value terms are appended to

Returns:

None

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_opf.add_corrective_contingency_formulation(t_idx: int, c: int, Sbase: float, contingency: LinearMultiContingency, contingency_flows: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[object_]], changed_idx: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[int64]], branch_data_t: PassiveBranchData, branch_vars: BranchNtcVars, vsc_vars: VscNtcVars, hvdc_vars: HvdcNtcVars, prob: PulpLpModel | OrToolsLpModel, corrective_rows: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[bool]], vsc_active: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[bool]] | None = None, hvdc_active: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[bool]] | None = None, vsc_delta_vars: Dict[int, LpVariable | Variable] | None = None, hvdc_delta_vars: Dict[int, LpVariable | Variable] | None = None, add_exchange_preservation: bool = True, enforce_rows: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[bool]] | None = None) → float | LpAffineExpression | LinearExpr[source]

Formulate a single contingency allowing corrective re-dispatch of the VSC and HVDC converters Rationale: VSCs and HVDCs can change their powers quickly after the contingency

For each non-outaged converter d we introduce a per-contingency set-point change Δ_d and write the post-contingency monitored flow as:

f_c[m] = f0[m] + MLODF[m, βδ]·f0[βδ] + Σ_d cDF[m, d]·Δ_d

where cDF is the post-contingency converter distribution factor. The post-contingency converter flow flow0_d + Δ_d is bounded by the converter rate. Δ_d carries no objective cost, so it is a pure feasibility (corrective) lever.

Parameters:

  • t_idx – time index being formulated

  • c – contingency (group) index, used to build unique variable/constraint names

  • Sbase

  • contingency – the linear multi-contingency providing the outaged indices and the compensated factors

  • contingency_flows – per-branch preventive post-contingency flow expressions

  • changed_idx – indices of the branches whose flow changes under the outage itself

  • branch_data_t – passive branch data

  • branch_vars – branch LP variable container

  • vsc_vars – VSC LP variable container

  • hvdc_vars – HVDC LP variable container

  • prob – linear problem the variables and constraints are added to

  • corrective_rows – per-branch flag, True for the branches whose corrective term is read back

  • vsc_active – in-service flag per VSC, or None to treat every VSC as in service

  • hvdc_active – in-service flag per HVDC, or None to treat every HVDC as in service

  • vsc_delta_vars – persistent per-VSC Δ variable store for this contingency, or None for a fresh one

  • hvdc_delta_vars – persistent per-HVDC Δ variable store, same rationale

  • add_exchange_preservation – add the exchange-preservation equality

  • enforce_rows – per-branch flag restricting which rows get their limit constraint

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_opf.add_corrective_control_effort(prob: PulpLpModel | OrToolsLpModel, vsc_delta_store: Dict[int, Dict[int, LpVariable | Variable]], hvdc_delta_store: Dict[int, Dict[int, LpVariable | Variable]], counted: Set[Tuple[int, int, int]], effort: List[LpAffineExpression | LinearExpr]) → None[source]

Append |Δ| for every corrective converter set-point change not yet counted, weighted 1 + 1e-3 x converter index to resolve equal-effort alternatives.

None

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_opf.compute_vsc_pmode3_saturation_rates(vsc_data_t: VscData, branch_data_t: PassiveBranchData, bus_data_t: BusData) → ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]][source]

Compute the effective P-mode 3 saturation rate of each VSC in MW. A P-mode 3 droop saturates when the converter cannot deliver more power, and that limit is the converter rating or the total rating of the DC branches attached to the converter’s DC bus, whichever is lower.

Parameters:

  • vsc_data_t – VscData structure

  • branch_data_t – PassiveBranchData structure (contains the DC lines)

  • bus_data_t – BusData structure (provides the is_dc marker)

Returns:

array of effective saturation rates (MW) per VSC

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_opf.evaluate_corrective_flow_addons(multi_contingencies: List[LinearMultiContingency], group_indices, vsc_delta_store: Dict[int, Dict[int, LpVariable | Variable]], hvdc_delta_store: Dict[int, Dict[int, LpVariable | Variable]], n_vsc: int, n_hvdc: int, n_branch: int, model: PulpLpModel | OrToolsLpModel) → Dict[int, ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]][source]

Evaluate the numeric branch flow change of every group’s solved corrective Δ set-points.

Each addon is compensated_df · Δ in per unit.

Parameters:

  • multi_contingencies – formulated multi-contingencies in LP order

  • group_indices – formulated-group positions to evaluate

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_opf.fill_worst_contingency_per_branch(grid: MultiCircuit, multi_contingencies: LinearMultiContingencies | None, f0_mw: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], hvdc0_mw: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], vsc0_mw: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], inj0_mw: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], contingency_rates_mw: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], alpha: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], worst_idx: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[int64]], worst_flow: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], worst_loading: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], alpha_n1_worst: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], tied_groups: List[Tuple[int, int, float, float, float]], branch_data: PassiveBranchData, solved_flows: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | ndarray[tuple[int, int], dtype[float64]] | CompactContingencies | None = None, corrective_addons_mw: Dict[int, ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]] | None = None) → None[source]

For every branch, keep the contingency group that maximises post-contingency loading.

The N-state loading is the starting point. A group is recorded only when its N-1 loading is worse by more than 1e-4 p.u., so an unaffected line keeps index -1 and N-1 flow = N flow. Ties go to the group that comes first in the grid.

Parameters:

  • grid – circuit that owns the contingency groups

  • multi_contingencies – formulated multi-contingencies, or None when N-1 is off

  • f0_mw – solved N-state branch flows (MW)

  • hvdc0_mw – solved N-state HVDC flows (MW)

  • vsc0_mw – solved N-state VSC flows (MW)

  • inj0_mw – solved N-state bus injections (MW)

  • contingency_rates_mw – branch contingency ratings (MW)

  • alpha – N-state exchange sensitivity of every branch

  • worst_idx – output, group index per branch, filled in place

  • worst_flow – output, N-1 flow (MW) of the worst group, filled in place

  • worst_loading – output, |N-1 flow| / contingency rate, filled in place

  • alpha_n1_worst – output, exchange sensitivity under the worst group, filled in place

  • tied_groups – output, (branch, group index, N-1 flow MW, N-1 loading p.u., alpha N-1) of the twin outages tied with the branch worst, filled in place

  • branch_data – passive branch data, to recognise the twin outages

  • solved_flows – solved physical contingency branch flows (groups x branches, MW), if available

  • corrective_addons_mw – per formulated group position, the solved corrective converter redispatch flow change (MW)

Returns:

None

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_opf.screen_contingency_violations(multi_contingencies: List[LinearMultiContingency], admitted_rows: Dict[int, ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[bool]]], f0: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], hvdc0: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], vsc0: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], inj0: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], monitorable: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[bool]], con_rates_pu: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], tol_pu: float, at_risk_fraction: float, delta_flow_addons: Dict[int, ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]] | None = None) → List[Tuple[int, ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[int64]]]][source]

Numerically evaluate every contingency group against a solved operating point and return, per violated group, the rows to admit into the LP. This accelerates the calculation quite a lot.

Parameters:

  • multi_contingencies – list of LinearMultiContingency

  • admitted_rows – per group index, boolean mask of the rows already in the LP

  • f0 – solved branch flows (p.u.)

  • hvdc0 – solved HVDC flows (p.u.)

  • vsc0 – solved VSC flows (p.u.)

  • inj0 – solved bus injections (p.u.)

  • monitorable – per-branch flag of branches that may get a post-contingency limit

  • con_rates_pu – branch contingency ratings (p.u.)

  • tol_pu – feasibility tolerance (p.u.) added to the rating before flagging

  • at_risk_fraction – fraction of the rating above which a row of a violated group is admitted preventively along with the violated rows

  • delta_flow_addons – per group index, the numeric flow change caused by that group’s solved corrective Δ set-points (compensated DF · Δ)

Returns:

list of (group index, row indices to admit)

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_opf.solve_least_control_effort(prob: PulpLpModel | OrToolsLpModel, objective: LpAffineExpression | LinearExpr, transfer: LpVariable | Variable, effort: List[LpAffineExpression | LinearExpr], logger: Logger, robust: bool, show_logs: bool, progress_text: None | Callable[[str], None]) → int[source]

Second stage. Among the solutions that reach the first stage TTC, take the one with the least control effort. This makes the reported operating point and its limiting pairs reproducible instead of an arbitrary optimal vertex.

The TTC is held exactly by fixing the transfer variable through its bounds, which the solver honours without tolerance. The limit slack penalties stay in the objective and the effort is added with a 1e-3 weight. A slack costs 1e4 per p.u., so 1 MW of limit relaxation outweighs 1e7 MW of control effort.

Parameters:

  • prob – linear problem solved at the first stage optimum

  • objective – first stage objective expression (transfer and limit slack penalties)

  • transfer – area 1 increase, the variable the TTC is maximised through, declared with bounds [0, inf)

  • effort – weighted absolute-value effort terms

  • logger – logger for the fallback warning

  • robust – robust solver mode

  • show_logs – display the solver logs

  • progress_text – GUI text callback

Returns:

solver status

  • monitor_only_sensitive_branches – only monitor branches sensitive enough

  • ntc_load_rule – fraction of the rating reserved to the exchange (ACER rule)

  • alpha_threshold – minimum N-1 exchange sensitivity for a branch to be monitored

  • alpha_n1_abs – absolute N-1 exchange-sensitivity matrix indexed as (branch, outaged-branch)

  • prob – linear problem the constraints are added to

Returns:

always 0.0

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.NTC.ntc_results.worst_contingency_report_table(time_array: ~pandas.core.indexes.datetimes.DatetimeIndex | None, branch_names: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.str_]], group_names: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.str_]], group_device_names: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.object_]], worst_idx: ~numpy.ndarray, worst_flow: ~numpy.ndarray, worst_loading: ~numpy.ndarray, alpha: ~numpy.ndarray, alpha_n1: ~numpy.ndarray, monitor_logic: ~numpy.ndarray, flow_n: ~numpy.ndarray, loading_n: ~numpy.ndarray, ttc: ~numpy.ndarray, contingency_rates: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.float64]], loading_threshold_pct: float, total_slack_mw: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.float64]] | None = None, time_percentage: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.float64]] | None = None, original_time_indices: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.int64]] | None = None, result_type: ~VeraGridEngine.enumerations.ResultTypes = Ntc: Contingency flow report, vsc_names: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.str_]] | None = None, vsc_power: ~numpy.ndarray | None = None, hvdc_names: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.str_]] | None = None, hvdc_power: ~numpy.ndarray | None = None, phase_shifter_indices: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.int64]] | None = None, phase_shift: ~numpy.ndarray | None = None, transmission_reliability_margin: float = 0.0, tied_groups: ~typing.List[~typing.Tuple[int, int, int, float, float, float]] | None = None, tie_time_keys: ~numpy.ndarray[tuple[~typing.Any, ...], ~numpy.dtype[~numpy.int64]] | None = None) → ResultsTable[source]

Build the long form worst-contingency table with one row per kept (time, branch).

A row is kept only when the branch is monitored and its N-1 loading or its N-state loading is at least loading_threshold_pct, so base-case limits show up as rows without a contingency group. We also handle tied groups. That is the NTC “loading threshold to report” option. It avoids allocating an object cell for every branch of every hour.

Parameters:

  • time_array – timestamps, or None for a snapshot

  • branch_names – branch names

  • group_names – contingency group names in grid order

  • group_device_names – joined outaged-device names in the same order

  • worst_idx – worst group index per time and branch, -1 if none

  • worst_flow – N-1 flow (MW) of that group

  • worst_loading – N-1 loading (p.u.) of that group

  • alpha – N-state exchange sensitivity

  • alpha_n1 – N-1 exchange sensitivity of the worst group

  • monitor_logic – N-state monitor flag

  • flow_n – N-state branch flow (MW)

  • loading_n – N-state branch loading over the normal rating (p.u.)

  • ttc – Optimized total transfer capacity of each time index (MW).

  • transmission_reliability_margin – Margin subtracted from TTC to report NTC (MW).

  • contingency_rates – branch contingency ratings (MW)

  • loading_threshold_pct – keep rows whose N-1 or N loading is at least this percent

  • total_slack_mw – optional total thermal slack per displayed operating point

  • time_percentage – optional cluster probabilities expressed as percentages

  • original_time_indices – optional original-series indices for the displayed hours

  • vsc_names – converter names, in stored power order

  • vsc_power – base operating-point converter powers, MW (time, converter)

  • hvdc_names – HVDC names, in stored power order

  • hvdc_power – base operating-point HVDC powers, MW (time, HVDC)

  • phase_shifter_indices – indices of branches configured for phase-angle control

  • phase_shift – base operating-point branch tap angles, radians (time, branch)

  • result_type – report title to display

  • tied_groups – (time key, branch, group, N-1 flow MW, N-1 loading p.u., alpha N-1) of the groups tied with the worst group of that time and branch

  • tie_time_keys – per displayed time row, the time key used in tied_groups (None when the keys are the displayed rows themselves)

Returns:

results table

get_solution_states(slack_tol_mw: float = 0.1) → List[SolutionState][source]

Classify each time step as Optimal, Relaxed, or NotOptimal.

Optimal: the solver converged and total slack is within tolerance. Relaxed: the solver converged, but only by relaxing limits. NotOptimal: the solver did not reach optimality.

Parameters:

slack_tol_mw – total slack below which the hour counts as clean

Returns:

one solution state per time step

get_total_slack_mw() → ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]][source]

Total limit-relaxation slack of each time step in MW.

Base-case overload slacks plus post-contingency relaxation slacks. Strict runs have no flow slacks, so the result is zero per hour.

Returns:

slack per time step in MW
